hints: Focus on what relative molecular mass really means, mass of one mole, so you need moles from a gas volume.
Notice the 22.4 dm3 value is only true at 0 C, so first shrink the 0.025 dm3 measured at 100 C down to 0 C using Kelvin temperatures 373 K and 273 K.
Combine mass divided by moles with that temperature correction to build the full expression for Mr and match it to the options.
walkthrough:
**Recall what Mr means**

Think of Mr as grams per mole. You have the mass, 0.10 g, so you just need the number of moles in that 0.025 dm3 of vapour.

$$M_r = \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{moles}}$$

**Correct the volume to 0 C**

Gas expands when heated, so 0.025 dm3 at 100 C would be smaller at 0 C. Always use Kelvin for gas laws.

$$T_1 = 100 + 273 = 373 \text{ K}, \quad T_2 = 0 + 273 = 273 \text{ K}$$

$$\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}$$

$$V_{\text{at 0 C}} = 0.025 \times \frac{273}{373}$$

**Find moles then Mr**

At 0 C, 1 mol occupies 22.4 dm3, so divide your corrected volume by 22.4 to get moles.

$$\text{moles} = \frac{V_{\text{at 0 C}}}{22.4} = \frac{0.025 \times 273}{373 \times 22.4}$$

Now put it into the Mr expression:
$$M_r = \frac{0.10}{\text{moles}} = \frac{0.10 \times 373 \times 22.4}{0.025 \times 273}$$

**Pick the matching formula**

That final arrangement has 0.10, 373 and 22.4 on top, with 0.025 and 273 below. That is exactly one of the options.

options.A: Incorrect. This inverts both the mass/volume ratio and the temperature ratio. It puts 0.025 on top and 0.10 below, and uses 273/373 instead of 373/273, giving a tiny value instead of Mr.
options.B: Incorrect. This gets the temperature correction the right way round (373 on top, 273 below) but still has mass and volume upside down. Mr = mass/moles, so mass must be on top.
options.C: Incorrect. This gets mass on top correctly but inverts the temperature correction. Hot gas occupies a larger volume, so to go from 100 C to 0 C you multiply by 273/373, which means 373 must end up on top in the final Mr expression.
options.D: Correct. Mass 0.10 g is on top, volume 0.025 dm3 is below, molar volume 22.4 converts corrected volume to moles, and 373/273 corrects from 100 C (373 K) back to 0 C (273 K). This gives $M_r = (0.10 \times 373 \times 22.4)/(0.025 \times 273)$.
